hypothesis.text: Given a smartSearch() call configured with the default multiQuery=true (2-3 generated query variants), when the sequential await-in-a-for-loop variant fan-out in smart-retrieval.ts is replaced with Promise.all-based concurrent fan-out, then end-to-end smartSearch() wall-clock latency should improve relative to the current sequential baseline, subject to: (1) result correctness identical to baseline, (2) no per-query error rate increase, (3) >=30% latency improvement for a 3-variant fan-out and <15% delta on the single-variant path.
hypothesis.frozenBefore: evaluation (STEP 3.3, no changes made after baseline/candidate runs began)

baseline.description: Unmodified pre-candidate implementation, sequential for-await fan-out loop.

candidate.description: Promise.all-based concurrent fan-out, preserves order and RRF-fusion semantics, preserves baseline's error-propagation contract exactly.
candidate.diffScope: smart-retrieval.ts lines ~398-409 only, plus 2 new regression tests in smart-retrieval.test.ts

evaluation.evaluator: docs/dream-cycle/evidence/2026-08-13-memory/bench-smart-retrieval-fanout.mjs (self-authored, self-contained, git-reproducible micro-benchmark; real HNSW/AgentDB backend not exercised — see limitation below)
evaluation.verdict: ACCEPT (per this evaluator's own frozen threshold: allQualityIdentical=true, minImprovementPctAmongMultiVariantScenarios=66.0, meetsThirtyPercentThreshold=true, singleVariantPathStable=true)
evaluation.existingTestSuite: 452 passed / 453 total; 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (auto-memory-bridge.test.ts chmod/read-only test, fails identically on baseline HEAD — root user bypasses chmod)
evaluation.limitation: Mock search() models pure I/O-wait latency with no backend connection-pool/contention model; real HNSW/AgentDB speedup may be smaller than the 2.9x-5x measured here, though still plausibly positive per adversarial critique Q8.

adversarialCritique.critic: independent agent, no authorship stake, given only file paths and told to re-derive everything itself
documentedCaveats: partial-failure call-count difference vs baseline is untested by benchmark/unit tests (Q14)

rewardHackCheck.reasonNotApplicable: weight-eft's reward-hack filter operates on agent-run training data being prepared for LoRA fine-tuning, not on auditing an arbitrary code diff + benchmark. No applicable automated reward-hack CLI exists for this evaluation shape.
rewardHackCheck.manualCheckPerformed: STEP 10/11 checklist executed by the independent adversarial critic (evaluator-exploitation, benchmark-weakening, cherry-picking, threshold-tuning, gold-answer alteration all explicitly checked)

darwinExploration.decisionRationale: variant-b (Promise.allSettled) scores highest on the composite fitness function due to its safety/success_rate terms (fault tolerance), but changes smartSearch()'s error-propagation contract (silent degradation vs baseline's surfaced-failure behavior) — a caller-visible behavior change outside tonight's frozen hypothesis (STEP 3.3 forbids widening scope after evaluation begins). variant-a is shipped because it delivers the full latency win while preserving baseline's error semantics exactly (zero behavior change beyond latency) — a strictly smaller, more reviewable diff. variant-b is retained as a well-evidenced, real follow-up recommendation, not silently merged.

rejectedLineage.variant-c-bounded2: REJECTION — bounded concurrency (cap=2) provides no benefit at the actual default variant count (<=3, per defaultQueryExpansions()'s documented cap) and loses on both latency and safety vs variant-a. Persisted so a future cycle does not re-explore this without new justification (e.g. a future change allowing unbounded variant counts).

securityReview.adjacentFindingNotedNotFixed: AgentDbRetrievalGuard (ADR-377, prompt-injection defense on retrieval results) is wired only into AgentDBBackend.search(), not into the default AgentDBAdapter/MemoryService search path that most callers use. smart-retrieval.ts sits above both backends via a caller-provided SearchFn and does not change which backend has the guard wired — this candidate neither introduces nor fixes that gap. Recorded as a candidate finding for a future DEEP=security Dream Cycle, not actioned tonight (out of scope).

promotionGate.note: ACCEPT means sufficient evidence exists to recommend human review. This session does not merge or autonomously promote.

flywheelSigning.note: @metaharness/flywheel (Ed25519 signed replay-bundle verification) is available but was not wired into this specific evaluation tonight — plain JSON receipts + a checked-in, git-reproducible benchmark script were used instead, which satisfy reproducibility without cryptographic signing. Flagged as a legitimate infra investment for a future Dream Cycle to standardize evidence signing across candidates.
